definition: A Walt Disney Imagineering employee; the company says it spans more than 100 disciplines, not only artists.
The hybrid creative-and-management role that owns an attraction's creative content through design and installation.
A creative role that turns concept art into dimensioned plans, elevations and models of scenes that can be built.
The illustrator who produces the key paintings and sketches that define how an attraction looks and feels.
The writer responsible for an attraction's story bible, scripts, signage copy and character voice.
An engineer who designs the vehicle, track and drive systems and proves they stay inside force and clearance limits.
An engineer who programs the PLC and safety logic that moves vehicles between block zones and stops them when sensors disagree.
A show technology role that writes the cue logic linking ride position to lights, audio, media, effects and figures.
The animator who authors an animatronic figure's movements and timing against the show's audio and ride cues.
A planning role that lays out lands, capacities, circulation and phasing for a whole park or resort.
A production role that builds and maintains the project schedule across design, fabrication and installation.
Deep ability in one craft plus working knowledge of the neighbouring disciplines, the profile themed entertainment teams hire for.
A portfolio that shows sketches, options and decisions for each project, not only finished renders.
The habit of tracing how one design change moves throughput, cost, pacing and safety before committing to it.
Walt Disney Imagineering's student design competition, started by Marty Sklar in 1991, with Hong Kong and Shanghai editions.
A US university competition in which teams design and build a working model attraction to a shared prompt over six months.
Toronto Metropolitan University's invitational student design contest held around IAAPA Expo since 2014.
The Themed Entertainment Association, the trade body for the companies and people who design and build experiences.
TEA's programme for students and early-career professionals, including a six-month mentorship and discounted event entry.
The International Association of Amusement Parks and Attractions, the operators' and suppliers' trade body that runs the Expos.
IAAPA's Certified Attractions Professional and Certified Attractions Executive credentials, earned by exam and maintained with continuing education.
TEA's signature conference on experience design, held regionally each year.
TEA's annual awards for outstanding achievement in themed entertainment, first presented in 1994.
The free three-lesson Khan Academy course on theme park design that Disney Imagineering released in 2020.
A front-line internship at Walt Disney World for enrolled US college students, a common first step into the industry.
